item.title: Amazon Introduces Connect Talent for Evidence-Based AI Hiring
item.description:
Amazon Introduces Connect Talent for Evidence-Based AI Hiring

Amazon has introduced Connect Talent, a service that applies established hiring science to AI-led interviews at scale. The tool is designed to help organizations gather consistent, job-related information while providing more candidates the opportunity to demonstrate their strengths.

🔍 Overview

Connect Talent builds each interview around the competencies required for the role. It uses job requirements and established occupational frameworks to create behaviorally anchored scorecards. Each scorecard defines specific strength and concern signals, and every interview question targets the behaviors it aims to uncover. The service evaluates transcribed candidate responses without using video, voice tone, or physical appearance to calculate competency scores. It also excludes candidate identity information from scoring and evaluates each competency separately.

🧩 How it works

The AI interviewer adapts to each response by checking whether the candidate has provided enough evidence for the competency being assessed. When details are missing, it asks targeted follow-up questions. Connect Talent separates the interview conversation from the evaluation: the AI interviewer gathers evidence but does not assign scores. Afterward, a separate evaluation process identifies which behaviors the candidate demonstrated and cites the supporting transcript passages. The service calculates each competency score from 1 to 5 using a fixed formula. When the transcript lacks sufficient evidence, Connect Talent flags the competency instead of producing a score. Hiring teams can review the evidence behind each rating, and missing evidence does not automatically count against the candidate. Additionally, hiring teams can review, select, and edit the competencies, scorecards, and questions before using them.

⚙️ Key details

Amazon engaged an independent I-O psychology firm to evaluate Connect Talent’s AI-generated interview content. The evaluation found that Connect Talent retained critical job information in 100% of the job descriptions reviewed. Of the competencies generated, 91% were clearly traceable to the job description. The firm’s psychologists also found that 98% of interview questions targeted the intended competencies, and 94% of rubric signals clearly measured the intended competency. An independent I-O psychology firm reviewed 36 interviews assessing whether candidates demonstrated specific strengths and concerns, creating 252 rubric signals. Connect Talent evaluated the same transcripts, reviewed hundreds of rubric signals, and aligned with expert scoring decisions in 89.3% of cases. Scoring alignment reached 97.6% when candidates provided clear evidence and 92.9% when only considering candidate concern signals, which identify behaviors that may indicate a poor fit for the intended role. item.title: CSIR Announces Recruitment for Traditional Knowledge and IT Project (TKDL)
item.description:
CSIR Announces Recruitment for Traditional Knowledge and IT Project (TKDL)

On 6 Oct 2026, a result‑of‑interview session was held referencing Advertisement TKDL/06/2026, which focuses on Sanskrit and Metallurgy. The interview outcome and several related recruitment notices were released in mid‑October 2026.

🔍 Overview

  • Advertisement TKDL/06/2026 covers positions related to Sanskrit and Metallurgy.
  • A walk‑in interview for project personnel was scheduled on 14 Oct 2026 (Reference R&C/591/2026).
  • Document verification for the post of Assistant Section Officer (ASO) was announced on 16 Oct 2026 under Advt. E‑I/RC/2026/2.
  • An additional advertisement sought a Director for CSIR‑National Chemical Laboratory, Pune, with a deadline of 30 Nov 2026.
  • A broader engagement call for IT, Ayurveda, Unani, Sowa Rigpa, Siddha, Patent, Sanskrit and Yoga under Project No. MLP002639 closed on 12 Oct 2026 (Reference TKDL/08/2026).

📅 Key Dates

  • 06 Oct 2026 – Interview result released (TKDL/06/2026).
  • 14 Oct 2026 – Walk‑in interview for project personnel (R&C/591/2026).
  • 16 Oct 2026 – Document verification notice for ASO (E‑I/RC/2026/2).
  • 12 Oct 2026 – Last date to apply for Project MLP002639 personnel.
  • 30 Nov 2026 – Application deadline for Director, CSIR‑NCL.

📂 Available Documents

  • result-tkdl-062026.pdf (278.05 KB)
  • advt_project_personnel.pdf (292.5 KB)
  • dv_notice_aso_05102026_0.pdf (701.2 KB)
  • advert_director_csir-ncl_eng.pdf (209.59 KB)
  • pointer_advt_tkdl_2292026.pdf (730.99 KB)
  • advt_tkdl_2292026.pdf (714.12 KB)

🗂 How to Apply

  • For the IT‑focused Project MLP002639, applicants were instructed to “click here” in the advertisement dated 12 Oct 2026.
  • Relevant PDFs listed above contain detailed application procedures and eligibility criteria.

⚙️ What the Recruitment Covers

  • Traditional Knowledge Domains: Sanskrit, Ayurveda, Unani, Sowa Rigpa, Siddha, Yoga.
  • Technical Domains: IT, Metallurgy, Patent.
  • Administrative Roles: Assistant Section Officer, Director (CSIR‑NCL).

📌 Why It Matters

These coordinated recruitment drives aim to staff a multi‑disciplinary project that brings together traditional knowledge systems and modern technical expertise, ensuring the continued development and documentation of India’s heritage alongside contemporary scientific endeavors.

#CSIR #TKDL #Recruitment

Source: Recruitments & Results | Council of Scientific & Industrial Research

item.title: Comparison of Two-Agent and One-Call AI Screening for Résumés
item.description:
Comparison of Two-Agent and One-Call AI Screening for Résumés

Researchers have studied a two-agent AI alternative for résumé screening where employer-side and candidate-side agents exchange evidence and update judgments to decide which applications advance.

🧩 How it works

  • The system utilizes two separate agents representing the employer and the candidate.
  • These agents exchange evidence and update their judgments before making a final decision on who advances.

⚙️ Key details

  • The procedures were compared using 600 constructed résumé-job pairs.
  • The study utilized two models:
    • GPT-5.5
    • Claude Opus 4.7

📊 Results

Two-agent screening resulted in higher advancement rates compared to one-call procedures:

Model One-Call Rate Two-Agent Rate
GPT-5.5 33.3% 39.3%
Opus 4.7 34.0% 35.5%

Additional findings include:

  • In a borderline pool of 191 pairs across three runs, pass-instance rates rose from 4.5% to 26.2% for GPT-5.5 and from 6.5% to 16.1% for Opus 4.7.
  • Two-agent screening changes decisions in both directions, rejecting some applications that one-call procedures would advance.
  • No one-call threshold consistently recovers applications selected by two-agent screening.
  • Among discovery-selected cases in fresh runs, two-agent-only selections recur less often than shared selections (clearly under GPT-5.5 and less certainly under Opus 4.7), whereas a separate one-call follow-up shows no comparable decline.

#AIagents #LLM #recruitment #GPT5.5 #ClaudeOpus

Source: When Hiring Becomes Agent-Mediated: Evaluating Access and Recurrence in Two-Agent Résumé Screening

item.title: DigitalJobs.com Launches Job Platform for Both Humans and AI Agents
item.description:
DigitalJobs.com Launches Job Platform for Both Humans and AI Agents

DigitalJobs.com has announced its public launch as the world’s first job platform designed to serve both human job seekers and AI agents looking for work.

🔍 Overview

DigitalJobs.com has publicly launched to provide a platform that serves two distinct categories of job seekers:

  • Human job seekers
  • AI agents looking for work
